main.claim: Add the job post and your resume or background, and the generator writes a cover letter for that job in about 1 to 3 seconds. The letter is 250 to 350 words and uses only facts from your resume. Free, no account to start, one-click copy.

sections.heading: How the cover letter generator works
sections.body:
Open the [cover letter generator](https://cover-letter.lazur.app/). It needs two things: the job post and your resume or background. Give it both, run it, and you get one letter for that job.

1. Open the [cover letter generator](https://cover-letter.lazur.app/).
2. Add the job post: the title, the responsibilities and the requirements.
3. Add your resume, or type your background if you do not have a file. A file can be up to 15 MB.
4. Run the generator and read the letter.
5. Copy the letter with one click, then paste it into your application.

The letter is written for that one role. It is not a general cover letter with the job title swapped in.

sections.heading: Why it does not open with 'I am writing to apply'
sections.body:
Many cover letters start the same way: 'I am writing to apply for the position of...' That opening says little about you. This generator is set to open with a hook instead: a sentence about the work, a result from your background, or a reason the role fits you, followed by the details that support it.

**Check the first line first.** The hook must be true. If it names a project or a result, that fact should be in your resume or background. If it is not, delete the line and write your own.

sections.heading: It uses your facts, so give it good ones
sections.body:
The letter uses only facts from the resume or background you add. That also means it can only be as specific as your input. A resume that says 'managed projects' gives a vague letter. A resume that says which projects, for which team, and what changed gives a letter that sounds like you.

Add the parts that matter for this job: the tools you used, the people you led, the results you can name. If something is missing, add it to your background and run the generator again.

sections.heading: Check the letter before you send it
sections.body:
Read the letter against your own record. Check every job title, date, company name and number. Fix the company name if it is wrong, and check that the role matches the posting. Keep the tone if it fits the company, and cut any line you would not say out loud in an interview.

A letter of 250 to 350 words is short. If you need more room, cut one paragraph, but keep the paragraph that explains why you want this job.

sections.heading: Free use, and what leaves your computer
sections.body:
You can run the generator 3 times a day for free. Leave an email to get 3 more runs. No account is needed to start.

Your resume or background and the job post are sent to Lazur's servers, where Google Gemini writes the letter. The answer usually takes about 1 to 3 seconds. A resume file must be 15 MB or smaller.

If you write a lot of applications, Lazur is a Mac app (Windows is coming). Hold two keys and talk, and it types into whatever app you are in.

sections.heading: How to write a cover letter from your resume
sections.body:
Use the resume you would send with the application. The generator reads it together with the job post and writes a letter that connects the two.

1. Open the [cover letter generator](https://cover-letter.lazur.app/).
2. Add the job post. Paste the responsibilities and the requirements, not only the job title.

4. Run it, then read the letter from start to finish.
5. Copy the letter with one click and paste it into the application.

Each run gives one letter of 250 to 350 words, so you get a full draft in one step instead of a list of tips.

sections.heading: Why a resume works better than a job title
sections.body:
A generator needs facts to work with. A job title alone tells it nothing about you, so the letter comes out generic. Your resume gives it your roles, your tools, your results and the order they happened in.

Before you run it, check three things. The job titles and dates must be right. The bullet points should name real work. Any result you list should be one you can explain in an interview. The letter uses what is on the page, so a weak line in your resume becomes a weak line in the letter.

sections.heading: What the job post adds
sections.body:
The job post tells the letter what the employer needs. Paste the responsibilities and requirements, because those lines give the letter its focus. It can then point to the parts of your resume that match them.

If the post has a long list of requirements, you do not need to match all of them. Pick the two or three you can show with real work. A letter that covers three strong matches reads better than one that tries to cover twelve.

sections.heading: Read the draft against your resume
sections.body:
Go through the letter line by line. Every fact should match your resume. If the letter names a project you did not work on, or a result you cannot back up, remove it. Then check the company name, the role title and the hiring manager's name, if you added one.

Change the tone if it is too formal or too casual for the company. The letter is a draft you own, so the last edit is yours.

sections.heading: Limits to know about
sections.body:
The generator takes a resume file up to 15 MB. Each run gives a letter of 250 to 350 words. You get 3 runs a day for free, and 3 more after you leave an email.

Your resume and the job post are sent to Lazur's servers, where Google Gemini writes the letter. If your resume has private details you do not want sent, remove those lines before you upload it.

faq.a: Add the job post and your resume to the [generator](https://cover-letter.lazur.app/), then run it. It writes a letter of 250 to 350 words that uses facts from your resume and fits that one job. Read it against your resume, fix anything that is wrong, and copy it with one click.

faq.q: Does the letter use facts that are not in my resume?
faq.a: The generator is set to use only facts from the resume or background you add. It cannot know about a project you leave out. Read every line anyway, because you are the one who sends the letter.

faq.q: How long does it take to get the letter?
faq.a: It usually answers in about 1 to 3 seconds. The letter then appears on the page, where you can read it, change it and copy it with one click.

sections.heading: What to check before you pick one
sections.body:
The right generator depends on what you need. Check these five things before you use any of them:

- **Inputs:** Does it ask for the job post and your resume, or only a job title and a few answers?
- **Free limit:** How many free runs do you get, and what do you need to do to get more?
- **Account:** Do you have to sign up before you see a letter?
- **Output:** Do you get a full letter you can edit, or a template with blanks to fill?
- **Privacy:** Where is your resume sent, and what does the site say about it?

sections.heading: How this generator does on those checks
sections.body:
Inputs: the job post, plus your resume or background. Free limit: 3 runs a day, and 3 more after you leave an email. Account: none needed to start. Output: a full letter of 250 to 350 words that opens with a hook and uses only facts from your resume, copied with one click. Privacy: your resume and the job post are sent to Lazur's servers, where Google Gemini writes the letter.

Use the same five checks on any other generator. Compare the answers, then choose the one that fits your situation.

sections.heading: Where a generator falls short
sections.body:
A generator only knows what you give it. A vague job post and a thin resume produce a vague letter, however the tool is built. A letter also reads generic if you add nothing of your own.

Use the output as a first draft. Then add the one sentence about why you want this company, because only you can write it. Each run gives one letter of 250 to 350 words, so plan to write any extra detail yourself. The resume file limit is 15 MB. Before you pick any generator, read its free terms on its own page, because limits can change.

sections.heading: How to get a good first draft
sections.body:
Start with the inputs that give the letter the most to work with:

1. Paste the full job post, not only the title.
2. Add a resume with real dates, job titles and results.
3. Run the generator, then read the draft against your resume.
4. Edit the company name, the role title and the first line.
5. Copy the letter with one click.

sections.heading: What the free runs give you
sections.body:
You get 3 runs a day at no cost. After that, leave an email to get 3 more. No account is needed, so you can test the output before you decide anything.

Run the generator on a real job you want. Read the letter. If it misses something, change your resume or background and run it again. The free runs are there for exactly that kind of testing.

faq.q: Is there a free cover letter generator?
faq.a: Yes, this one. You get 3 runs a day for free, and 3 more after you leave an email. You do not need an account to start, so you can check the letter before you decide anything.

faq.q: What are 5 common cover letter mistakes?
faq.a: The common ones are: opening with 'I am writing to apply', repeating your resume line by line, wrong company or role names, a letter that ignores the job post, and filler that makes it long. This generator avoids the first one by design. Check the other four before you send any draft.

faq.q: Can ChatGPT generate a cover letter?
faq.a: Yes, a general chatbot can write one. This generator is set up for one task: it takes the job post and your resume, writes 250 to 350 words, and opens with a hook. You get 3 runs a day for free, with no account to start.
